scope: Test the three extracted integrations with the PR's npmCheck/npmTest APIs and a local workspace-peer patch. Source is archived from the pinned commit; the supplied checkout is left untouched.
originalFinding: The original unpatched probe and results.json reproduce rejection of workspace:^ before any consumer assertions run.
workspaceHandling: Resolve workspace:^, workspace:~, workspace:*, and explicit workspace ranges to pnpm's packed declarations. Read historical peer versions from the same Git commit. Preserve optional peers and reject unresolved or unsupported workspace declarations.
additionalFix: Replace an installed candidate's version manifest atomically, preserving shared hard-linked cache files and other environments.
consumerMatrix: Eight frozen environments: React 18/19 and Solid 1.9 against released atom.io 0.53.3, plus React 18/19, Solid 1.9, and devtools with React 18/19 against Changesets-certified SDK 0.54.0 and integration 0.0.1 candidates.
checks: Consumer runtime behavior, strict declaration checks, physical peer identity, devtools CSS, rejection of missing candidate release evidence, and rejection of a deliberately broken packed React hook.
offlineSetup: ATOM_IO_PEER_STORE selects an existing pnpm store. This machine's sandbox run reuses immutable cached data through a writable /tmp index and materializes imported file links. No dependency versions or repository supply-chain policies are relaxed.
limitations: The firstRelease option isolates this current-consumer experiment; it does not certify the absence of a published release or replace the existing historical test gates.
Devtools is tested as a coordinated release with the React candidate; no released @atom.io/react environment is claimed.
The patch is carried here for evaluation and has not been applied to the upstream PR.

negativeControls: Missing SDK/React candidate release intent is rejected for all three integrations.
A deliberately broken packed React hook fails compatibility.
